source_name: AQP — Agjencia Qendrore e Prokurimit (Central Procurement Agency, Ministry of Finance)
why_relevant: Runs joint/framework procurements on behalf of all central and local contracting authorities, and publishes the signed contracts and decisions itself. Whole-of-government framework contracts (e.g. banking services, card/fuel-card style supplies, payment acceptance for public bodies) would run through here and state aggregate quantities.

source_name: BQK / CBK — Tenderet (Central Bank of Kosovo procurement notices)
why_relevant: The central bank operates the interbank payment system and is building a TIPS-clone instant-payments scheme; its own tender and award notices are the only public window on procurement of payment-switch, RTGS/instant-payment, cash-handling and currency-processing infrastructure. CBK publishes award notices as PDFs on its own site (own procurement rules in force since 01.12.2024) in addition to e-Prokurimi.

State-owned postal operator with counter networks and payment/bill-collection services — a realistic public buyer of POS terminals, cash-handling and counter payment systems. Publishes its own 'Njoftim per dhenie te kontrates' documents in parallel with e-Prokurimi.

source_name: Dogana e Kosovës — procurement announcement files (AnnouncementFiles)
why_relevant: Kosovo Customs collects duties at borders and offices and is a live buyer of card-acceptance/POS and cash-handling equipment. Hosts B08 and B52 notice PDFs on a predictable /sharedfolder/AnnouncementFiles/ path, which makes it one of the easiest buyer-side document stores to harvest and a good template for other rks-gov.net bodies.

Representative of the state-owned utility tier (alongside KEK/KESDS/water utilities) whose tenders cover metering, billing and customer-payment collection systems — the channel through which utility bill-payment and POS/kiosk infrastructure enters the market. Utilities are a major driver of cash-vs-card payment behaviour in Kosovo.

source_name: Zyra Kombëtare e Auditimit (National Audit Office of Kosovo) — audit reports
why_relevant: Annual regularity and performance audits of ministries, agencies and publicly-owned enterprises routinely dissect specific contracts, listing values, quantities delivered and implementation failures. Reports frequently expose payment-infrastructure and IT-system contracts in detail unavailable in the tender notice itself. NAO published 19 reports under the 2025/2026 audit plan (11 central, 7 local).

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP) + EBRD procurement notices
why_relevant: IFI channel: EBRD-financed clients in Kosovo (utilities, SOEs, financial-sector projects) must publish general and specific procurement notices with technical scope. Captures payment/IT infrastructure procurement that never reaches the national portal.

source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations — Procurement notices and contract awards (Kosovo)
why_relevant: World Bank-financed Kosovo operations (public finance, digital government, financial-sector) publish General Procurement Notices, Invitations for Bids and contract-award data including supplier and value. Contract-award datasets are also exposed via WBG Finances One, enabling structured extraction of vendors supplying payment/IT systems.

UNDP implements EU/IPA and bilateral projects in Kosovo under indirect management, running its own RFP/ITB procedures. Donor-funded digitalisation and financial-inclusion projects buy payment hardware, card/ID personalisation and e-payment integrations outside the national portal.

Second donor-implementer channel in Kosovo; IOM procures cash-assistance disbursement, prepaid-card and payment-service arrangements for beneficiary programmes, which reveal card issuing/acquiring capabilities of local banks and PSPs.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU Official Journal supplement)
why_relevant: Kosovo is not an EU member so its domestic notices are not on TED, but EU external-action and IPA service/supply contracts implemented for Kosovo, plus framework contracts naming Kosovo as place of performance, do appear. Also the place where EU-based vendors' Kosovo-adjacent payment contracts surface.

source_name: javne-nabavke.com — Kosovo region tender aggregator (Serbian language)
why_relevant: Commercial Serbian-language aggregator covering Kosovo tenders; provides the sr-language entry point (bankomati, POS terminali, platni promet) and a rough sense of volume — its own page reports over 8,000 Kosovo tenders published in 2023 at ~EUR 448k average estimated value. Useful for cross-language keyword discovery rather than as an authoritative record.

source_name: Municipal e-Prokurimi sub-portals (e.g. Komuna e Prishtinës)
why_relevant: All 38 municipalities publish their own procurement pages under the kk.rks-gov.net domain. Municipalities buy cash-desk/POS payment acceptance for tax and utility counters, parking payment systems and kiosk terminals — local-level payment-acceptance demand invisible in national statistics.

source_name: KALLXO.com (BIRN/KDI) — e-prokurimi and KRPP tag archives
why_relevant: Investigative outlet that continuously reports on specific Kosovo tenders, single-source awards, negotiated procedures without publication, and platform outages (e.g. the six-day e-Prokurimi outage). Best early-warning pointer to contracts worth pulling, and to periods where the portal record is incomplete.

source_name: Global Public Procurement Database (GPPD) — Kosovo (XK) country profile
why_relevant: World Bank-hosted harmonised procurement statistics for Kosovo — spend by category, procedure type and buyer. Provides the denominator and benchmark against which any ATM/POS contract volumes found in e-Prokurimi should be sized.

source_name: RKS Open Data portal — KRPP organisation datasets
why_relevant: Government open-data catalogue entry for the procurement regulator; the canonical place to discover any additional published procurement datasets/resources beyond the OCDS API, with Albanian/Serbian/English metadata.
